name: LEESER, Julian Martin

headline.note: The official chronology identifies a High Court associateship, private legal practice and political-staff roles before longer service at a party-aligned research centre and a university. It supplies mostly year-only boundaries and no hours, leave or substantive full-time evidence. Political staff, university and nonprofit work, governance, party activity, elected office, fellowship and study are excluded under the codebook. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.evidence_note: The current parliamentary biography records party membership from 1992 and offices including Berowra conference vice-president (2009–2016), Fox Valley branch secretary (2010–2016), Hornsby conference president (2014–2016) and NSW Division vice-president (2015–2016). It does not state remuneration or an employment relationship.
career_spells.counting_note: Party membership and organisational offices are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies list the two UNSW degrees but do not give enrolment or graduation dates, study load or overlap with council and party activity.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen and current parliamentary biographies establish 1995–1999 council service. Secondary chronology, citing Woollahra Council's alderman and councillor directory, supplies the election-day boundaries. The office overlapped university study and party activity.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Constitutional Convention delegate and member of the official government No Case Committee
career_spells.evidence_note: The parliamentary biography records election as a 1998 Constitutional Convention delegate and membership of the 1999 official government No Case Committee. The first speech corroborates the delegate and later campaign work. It does not establish employment, remuneration or hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Campaign and representative political activity are excluded from the employment headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen and current parliamentary biographies place the High Court associateship in 2000; Leeser's first speech identifies Justice Callinan as a former employer. Exact appointment dates, hours, leave and employment status are not published in the sources reviewed.
career_spells.counting_note: The public employer is established, but a year label and role title do not prove a countable full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Minister for Employment, Workplace Relations and Small Business, Tony Abbott MP
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies place the adviser role in 2001. Public sources reviewed do not supply exact dates, payroll basis, hours, leave or overlap with legal study or subsequent private practice.
career_spells.counting_note: Ministerial political staff work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Mallesons Stephen Jaques (now King & Wood Mallesons)
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary chronology identifies the firm, role and 2002–2004 years. Secondary and public event biographies corroborate the predecessor firm's current identity. Exact start/end dates, admission timing, hours, leave and any overlap with the adjoining adviser roles remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private legal employment is supported, but year-only boundaries and missing substantive full-time evidence prevent a headline duration.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Attorney-General, Philip Ruddock MP
career_spells.evidence_note: The official chronology places the special-adviser role from 2004 to 2006; a professional biography specifies constitutional law. Exact boundaries, payroll basis, hours, leave and the transition from Mallesons are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Ministerial political staff work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies give 2006–2012. A 2006 constitutional-society publication says Leeser had recently been appointed, his 2016 first speech describes running the centre for six and a half years, and a later professional biography confirms the same year range. The centre is a party-aligned policy institute; exact dates, hours, leave and legal employment terms remain unresolved. Contemporaneous employer-published 2009 book refines commencement to February 2006 and identifies the legal entity as Menzies Research Centre Limited, ACN 067 379 684. Funding does not change control coding.
career_spells.counting_note: Think-tank/nonprofit employment is displayed separately and excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.employer: Alfred A. Taubman Center for State and Local Government, Harvard Kennedy School
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and professional biographies identify the visiting fellowship in 2006–2007, overlapping the Menzies Research Centre role. They do not state appointment dates, location, funding, employment terms, hours or leave from Menzies.
career_spells.counting_note: The fellowship is treated as research/professional development and excluded; it is not assumed to be paid employment.

career_spells.role: Director, Government Policy and Strategy; senior executive
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract and current parliamentary biography record ACU senior-executive service from 2012 to 2016. Contemporary secondary synthesis, citing an ACU appointment notice, specifies the title and a July 2012 start; the ABC 2016 election guide says he held that role immediately before preselection. The exact start day, 2016 cessation date, hours, leave and campaign arrangement are unresolved. Employer annual report confirms replacement in mid-2016, but neither replacement timing nor election day is treated as the member’s exact employment cessation.
career_spells.counting_note: University employment is excluded from the narrow headline under the codebook, irrespective of seniority.

research_notes: The official occupation chronology is preserved without inferring continuous full-time work across year boundaries.
High Court service is public-sector employment and Mallesons is private-sector employment, but neither is converted to a duration because exact dates, hours and leave are missing.

Ministerial adviser roles are classified as political staff and excluded; Menzies Research Centre is classified as nonprofit/think-tank work and ACU as university work, also excluded under the codebook.
The 2006–2007 Harvard fellowship overlaps the Menzies role and is treated as fellowship/professional development, not presumed employment.
The undated official company-director label is linked cautiously to publicly identified nonprofit boards without inferring pay, workload or operational employment.

2026-10-01 follow-up: Menzies commencement refined to February 2006; original combined boards separated and Mercy Public Hospitals March 2015 appointment added without conflating the parent organisation. Added religious teaching/community roles, Ramsay scoping work and non-executive governance, and NLA parliamentary governance.

Searched legal-employer and court chronology, full-time wording, Menzies publications, ACU/Mercy annual reports, charity filings and library reports. Full-time searches found staff vacancies rather than evidence about Leeser. ACNC scanned report inspected visually after one copy failed retrieval. NLA old PDF redirects and archive failed; exact appointment day remains a labelled indexed lead. No supported High Court/Mallesons full-time interval, leave history or dates found.

Which legal offices and dates comprise the official company-director occupation, and were the Mercy Health, Teach For Australia or Playwriting Australia roles remunerated or operational?
What were the UNSW enrolment/graduation dates and overlaps with Woollahra Council, party and campaign activity?
Was the 2016 preselection/campaign remunerated, and when did ACU employment cease relative to the campaign and election?
Was the Ramsay founding study paid separately, by which entity, on what dates and hours, or undertaken within ACU employment?
What were the Ramsay board appointment/cessation dates and fees, and National Library Council reappointments and end?
Can separate Mercy Health and Mercy Public Hospitals appointments, teaching and community-governance dates and remuneration be established?
